declared_deviations_and_clarifications.text: T1 constant k: the registered formula mu = 2*s*(0.20/ann_vol)*one_way_cost gives mean |mu| 0.00031 per day and median 0.00037 per day, about 0.45x and 0.53x the one-way cost (0.0007), not the plan text 'median |mu| ~ 2x one-way cost'. 0.20/ann_vol is below 1 whenever annualised vol exceeds 20%. Consequence: only 2.5% of decisions have |mu| above the one-way cost, and T1 averaged 5.8% gross exposure with 24 trades. The registered formula was run as written, not recalibrated.

Funding timing: the funding rate of a due row (for example the 00:00 settlement) is treated as known at the 00:00 decision, under this dataset's available_at == timestamp convention (the independent reviewer checked all 48,912 x 5 rows).

Unregistered constant: BlendSource requires at least 30 finite pooled observations for the T1 and T3 trailing std (the Ridge24 minimum of 10 daily dates is registered). The 30 is not in the frozen constants.

T2 is a high-turnover signal (2,278 trades, turnover 57.6 in the base scenario, |mu| above the one-way cost on 70% of decisions); only T1 and T3 are low-turnover signals, T7 mostly sits flat after its latch, and T6/T8 trade less than the PR-C arms.

probe_rule_amendment.effect: the label flips: NO_WINNER under the PR-C rule (primary), DEVELOPMENT_PROMISING (T1) under the amended rule. Both are computed by code in trial_labels.py from the committed metrics plus the committed execution-1 probe outcomes.
observations_before_the_change_as_far_as: a partial real-data timing probe (execution 3, 2023-01-01..2023-03-01) printed T3 base terminal net profit 0.0%, which looks like no trading in that window
a synthetic-data test failed because trials that do not trade in a short window have causality_matrix passed=False under the trade requirement
the reasoning that the T3 |mu| (about 3e-4 per day) is below the one-way cost (7e-4), so T3 might not trade
probe_rule_amendment.rule_in_execution_1: PR-C rule: a per-arm causality probe passes only if the pre-cut decisions and traces are identical AND the arm traded before the cut (the registry text states no trade requirement; the requirement is inherited from the PR-C runner).
probe_rule_amendment.rule_in_execution_2: amended: identical decisions (per-decision expected-return vectors) and identical traces; trades are not required (as PR-C already allows for CASH).
probe_rule_amendment.what_the_real_data_later_showed: T3 DID trade before the 2023-07-01 cut (pre_cut_trace_has_trades=true); the only trial without pre-cut trades is T1 (mean |mu| 0.45x the one-way cost, 2.5% of decisions above it). No T1 replay or probe output had been seen when the change was made. It cannot be excluded that the amendment was influenced by the partial T3 observation, and a non-trading T1 was foreseeable from the registered formula (not computed beforehand).
